title: Judah's Trials and the Assyrian Conquest
english: …It has happened to them of the undesirable things. For Samaria has been destroyed, and the surrounding areas of the nations—Idumeans, Moabites, and those from Philistia—have trampled Judah. They have suffered many terrible things and have been tried by harsh days, both they and those. God will bring days that have not yet occurred, from the time when Ephraim separated from Judah (Hosea 8:9).

On that day, the Lord will hiss to the flies, which rule over the part of the river of Egypt, and to the bee, which is in the land of the Assyrians (Isaiah 7:18); and all will come and rest in the clefts of the land, and in the holes of the rocks, and in the caves, and in every hollow tree. The king of the Assyrians, that is, Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed Jerusalem and took all of Judah by force, burned the divine temple, and left nothing untouched, doing everything to the nation. The narrative is being sharpened, and it penetrates thinly into the onset of the war, and that all their land, villages, and cities will be distributed among those who come against them at the designated times.

Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, having left the one who was provoking, marched out with the entire army and was hastening against the land of the Assyrians. Josiah, being afraid that he might come against Judah, wanted to oppose him, although Pharaoh was dismissing the war against him. Rising up, he was killed in the war, and the Egyptian gained control of the land of the Judahites, and he came to such a degree of power that he even removed the reigning king, Joahaz, son of Josiah, and led him bound to his own land, and appointed Eliakim as king, and imposed taxes on the nation, and demanded a large collection of money.

Then, Eliakim, having reigned over Judah for eleven full years, was succeeded by his son, Jehoiachin. After him, Zedekiah reigned, during whose reign Nebuchadnezzar campaigned against Judah, and having destroyed all, and added Jerusalem to the other cities, he took Israel captive, along with the vessels…

title: Rejection of Necromancy
english: Those who speak from their belly are not a sensible nation towards God.
It is foolish for them to seek something from the living about the dead.
The law was given to help them, so that they might say what is right.
Emmanuel weaves a catechetical word for those who have hope in him, who were enrolled among children, and they were given to him by God and the Father, as Savior and Redeemer and Life-giver.
He completely separates them from ancient habits and the madness of the first, which included loving oracles from demons and clinging to certain necromancers who say nothing true.
Instead, he teaches them to seek God and learn from him, rather than accepting the counsel of those who speak from their own belly.
For they speak from their own belly, and they are not a sensible nation, so as to seek God and learn something from him.
You see how it works out foolishly: it not only commands to depart from their darkness and mind-destroying, but also to become good advisors to those who have been misled.
The common and human reasoning is to ask what the dead have to do with the living.
What kind of reasoning would it be to ask about the living from those in the earth or in Hades?

It is completely ignorant to pay attention to necromancy and the false boasts of sorcerers who have a dead mind and a frozen heart, for they do not know the creator of all things and do not have the life-giving word of God within them.
If someone were to come, saying, 'Seek those who speak from the earth, that is, those who pretend to bring up the dead; and as if making prophecies from Hades;', they should not accept their counsel.
The living, who have the heavenly life-giving power within themselves and have been enriched by the living word of God, ask what the dead have to do with the living.
They should say to those who counsel with them, 'What do they seek from the living about the dead?'

The law has been given as help, that is, the evangelical law, so that those who pay attention to it may say: 'Not like this word, for which no gifts can be given.', for those who speak from their own heart sell falsehood, but the saving and true law of God.

Ventriloquists, who pretend to have certain gods in their belly, so that they speak the things from them to those who come, and who make prophecies as if from Hades, do not know the creator of all things and do not have the life-giving word of God within them, and they are concerned with the works of the dead.

title: Rejection of the Old Covenant
english: Having been made manifest, those things were in praises to many.

The Bible tells us about Zechariah and Elizabeth, a priest and his wife who were descendants of Aaron, and how they were both righteous in God's eyes, following all of His commandments and laws without fault.

The apostle Paul, although saying openly that he was blameless according to the righteousness in the law, considered those things a loss for Christ, saying, 'But what was my gain? I have deemed these things a loss on account of Christ' (Philippians 3:7).

Before Christ came, some people who followed the law were strong and courageous, but after He appeared and the gospel was preached, the old ways of following the law came to an end, and the true, spiritual way of worshiping God began.
God is not pleased with the young men of the Jews who still choose to live according to the old law.
The sacrifices, baptisms, and observance of the Sabbath are no longer accepted by God.
We have been taught the way of living that pleases God.
The young men of the Jews who cling to the old ways are not pleasing to God, and their practices are rejected.

Those from Israel who oppose Christ have been deprived of true instruction, and as a result, their eyes have been darkened, and their backs have been bent, making them unable to look up towards heavenly things, but instead focused on earthly concerns.
The people who are in need of spiritual guidance and instruction are like orphans, and those who have become barren and unfruitful, lacking the teachings of God, are like widows.
They have become this way because they lack the one who provides all good teachings.
They will be convinced of this, not without reason, but because they have all become lawless and wicked, and every mouth speaks evil.
They are full of wickedness, having tried to kill the one who calls people to life, who did not know sin.
As the law says clearly, 'Will you not kill the innocent and the just?' (Exodus 23:7).
All the tongues of the Jews have spoken unjustly, crying out to Pilate, 'Away with him, away with him, crucify him!' (Matthew 27:22-23).
If this one is not killed...
